title: Opening day at the Palladium and the Prince of Wales arrives
summary: Backstage before the Palladium, the Prince of Wales interrupts a singer's act.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: We opened up at the Palladium, I'll never forget it. We did, they call it first and second house, and that's like a matinee in the afternoon. It's really the afternoon about three or four o'clock so we closed the first half of the program.

Now, we opened the first half -- the second half, all the others was English acts, so this big lady, she's a big star and I forget her name, big, big star, singer, she was in the middle of a song doing her act, so we were backstage-chasing -- in the dressing room, all you had to do was ring the bell and the waiter would come back and serve you, anything you wanted. That's the first time I ever saw that.

Them European acts were terrible. They was dead. They would tear you up. So the guys were nervous, you know, the guys walking up and down, you know, nervous, I say, 'Man, this is just another gig,' don't -- so Duke said, 'Press the button and bring all the boys a drink.' All of them had -- 'make them doubles.' So now this woman out here singing, and in the middle of the act, in the middle of the woman's song, right in the -- dead in the middle, the goddamn pit band goes into the National Anthem 'God Save the King,' or something, and every son of a bitch stood up. Them people around the curtain, I said, what happened, man, in walked the Prince of Wales. Now, I say, 'Man,' I never heard
no shit like this, this don't make no sense." He wasn't no bigger than this.
